newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai-Burma border tensions end, troops pull back.
newsitem.headline: Thai-Burma border tensions end, troops pull back.

text.p: A week of localised Thai-Burma border tension over Burmese dredging of a river ended on Thursday when troops from both sides withdrew, a Thai official said.
Both sides had agreed to discuss the border dispute at the government-to-government level, Lieutenant General Thanom Watchapuk, commander of Thailand's third army region, told reporters.
Tensions flared last Sunday when about 100 Burmese soldiers accompanied some workers to dredge and straighten part of the Moei River to reclaim some land as Burmese territory, the official said.
The Moei river is part of the 2,400-km (1,500-mile) Thai-Burma border and there have been long-standing localised disputes in the area because of some unclear demarcations.
The Burmese action prompted the Thai army to send hundreds of soldiers to the area to order the workers to stop the dredging. That forced a standoff between the two sides.
"My counterpart, General Khiet Seing, has ordered his troops to pull back, and we agreed to discuss the border problem at a higher level," Thanom said.
He was speaking after meeting Khiet Seing at this Thai border town.
Troops from both sides were seen shaking hands before the Burmese moved into their respective territory.
"We are friends and can settle problems at the negotiating table, not by force," a Thai unit commander told Burmese soldiers as they withdrew.
